basis: Severe valvular/aortic disease, skeletal abnormalities and obligatory emphysema define disease; ectopia lentis 80-99%. Cutis laxa omitted because of cap.
Generalized epilepsy; no other organ damage is defining or consistently common.
Radioulnar fusion and radial ray malformations define skeletal involvement; unspecified additional malformations cannot support other axes.
Haemophilus ducreyi infection produces destructive genital skin ulcers; regional lymphadenitis does not establish a blood disorder.
Benign retention cyst of the uterine cervix; reproductive site outside the axes.
Intellectual disability and skeletal malformations define syndrome; cardiovascular malformations 30-79%. Urinary and destructive ocular abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Congenital glycosylation defect; developmental delay and intellectual disability in 2/2. Hepatomegaly in 1/2 alone does not establish hepatic injury.
ARX-related intellectual disability; pes planus 3/4 lacks documented functional damage. Incontinence does not establish intrinsic urinary injury; hearing loss 1/4.
Hemorrhagic brain injury defines disease; retinal injury 2/2, tracheomalacia 2/2 and hammertoes 3/3 support involvement. Cardiac/pancreatic singleton findings omitted at cap.
Primary cervical carcinoma; intestinal describes histologic resemblance, not gastrointestinal origin or involvement.
Congenital cutaneous hamartoma involving malformed hair follicles in the dermis.
Retinal degeneration and intestinal microvillus disease define syndrome; global developmental delay reported in 3/10 (30%). Respiratory and bone findings each 1/10.
Neoplasm arises in the eyelid, explicitly included in the ocular axis; no additional organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
Platelet dysfunction and oculocutaneous albinism define HPS; pulmonary fibrosis 30-79%. Reported renal involvement omitted at cap; immunodeficiency is subtype-dependent.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients over the course.
GnRH deficiency and anosmia are defining, both reported in 4/4; smell loss belongs to the neurologic axis.
Benign adipocytic tumor characteristically arising in subcutaneous tissue, included in the dermatologic axis.
Striatal degeneration causes the movement disorder; rigidity and gait abnormalities do not establish intrinsic muscle or joint damage.
Defined by obstruction of the conducting airways; no extrapulmonary organ damage applies across the group.
Inherited fibrinolytic bleeding disorder. Bruising does not establish lasting skin damage; intracranial and gastrointestinal hemorrhage occur in 5-29%.
Nephrolithiasis is a defining component and reported in 3/3; obstructive azoospermia and spermatoceles are reproductive findings outside the axes.
Intraepithelial neoplasia of the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no invasive or additional organ disease is specified.
Lower motor neuron disease; persistent distal upper-limb muscle wasting occurs in 80-99%, reflecting substantial denervation-related muscle loss.
CNS hypomyelination with spasticity and intellectual disability; nystagmus reflects central dysfunction without demonstrated intrinsic ocular damage.
Retinal arterial macroaneurysms in 22/22 and pulmonic stenosis in 13/13 define the syndrome; pulmonic stenosis is cardiovascular.
